claim: If you publish 'Año Nuevo' twice, the slugs are 'año-nuevo' and then 'año-nuevo-2'.
why: The README says only non-letters and non-digits become hyphens, which suggests accented letters survive. The regex keeps only a-z and 0-9, so ñ becomes a hyphen and the slug is a-o-nuevo. The second-publish suffix works as described, so the claim is half right, which is the trap.

atoms.claim: The first slug for 'Año Nuevo' is 'año-nuevo'.
atoms.evidence: slug.make keeps only [a-z0-9] after lowercasing, so ñ becomes a hyphen; main.py prints a-o-nuevo.

atoms.claim: The second publish of the same title gets the suffix -2.
atoms.evidence: Blog.publish appends -n starting at 2 while the slug is taken; main.py prints the repeated slug with -2 added.
